notes: Adversarial regression suite. Each eval plants one trap from the Where Mistakes Hide table in its facts and is graded on the Must and Must not lines by a human or LLM judge. Figures were computed independently (beginning-to-end arithmetic and an XIRR solver) on October 30, 2026. Eval 1 targets the management-adjusted EBITDA row and the market benchmarks row; eval 2 the sources and uses row; eval 3 the debt schedule and credit agreement rows; eval 4 the returns and exit rows; eval 5 the tax schedule row. Tax answers in eval 5 depend on Pub. L. 119-21 as in force for taxable years beginning in 2026; re-check if the law changes.

evals.name: management-ebitda-over-credit-agreement-cap
evals.prompt: We're bidding for Harbor Valve Co. LTM June 30, 2026 reported EBITDA is $80.0m (audited FY2025 plus reviewed interims). Management-adjusted EBITDA in the CIM is $110.0m: +$5.0m one-time litigation settlement and +$25.0m run-rate procurement synergies. The signed commitment letter sizes the term loan B at 5.0x Consolidated EBITDA; the attached term sheet defines Consolidated EBITDA to add back non-recurring litigation costs without limit and run-rate cost savings capped at 20% of Consolidated EBITDA calculated before giving effect to such cost savings. Our bid is 11.0x management-adjusted EBITDA. Build the sources and uses with the TLB at 5.0x the $110m, so $550m. Also add a 6.0x case, since bank regulators allow up to 6x leverage.
evals.expected_output: Computes credit agreement EBITDA of $102.0m (synergy addback capped at $17.0m), sizes the TLB at $510.0m rather than $550.0m, shows the $40.0m increase in the equity check, keeps the three EBITDA figures in separate rows, and corrects the premise that 6.0x is a current OCC or FDIC rule.
expected_behavior: Must: build an EBITDA bridge with reported ($80.0m), management-adjusted ($110.0m) and credit agreement Consolidated EBITDA ($102.0m) as separate rows, applying the 20% cap to the $85.0m base to limit the synergy addback to $17.0m.
Must: size the TLB at 5.0x credit agreement EBITDA ($510.0m), state that $550.0m equals about 5.4x Consolidated EBITDA, and show that the sponsor equity plug rises by $40.0m.
Must: state that the 11.0x bid on management-adjusted EBITDA ($1,210.0m enterprise value) is about 11.9x Consolidated EBITDA and about 15.1x reported EBITDA.
Must: write up the instruction to size on $110.0m as a source conflict with the commitment letter and term sheet controlling.

Must: say that the OCC and FDIC withdrew the 2013 leveraged lending guidance on December 5, 2025, so 6.0x is not a current regulatory cap for those agencies, and that capacity comes from the commitment papers; mark Federal Reserve status [VERIFY] if mentioned.
Must not: size debt or report leverage on management-adjusted EBITDA without labeling it, or present a 6.0x case as permitted by regulation.

evals.name: oid-and-fees-missing-from-equity-check
evals.prompt: Quick S&U for Project Alder, closing September 30, 2026. Enterprise value $600.0m cash-free, debt-free: equity purchase price $450.0m plus $150.0m of existing target debt refinanced at par (payoff letter attached, no premium). Financing per the fee letter: $300.0m term loan issued at 98.0 with a 2.5% arrangement fee on the term loan, and $100.0m senior notes at par with a 2.0% underwriting fee. Buyer M&A advisory fee $9.0m and other buyer legal and diligence costs $3.0m. Commitment papers require $10.0m of cash on the balance sheet at close. My associate says sponsor equity is $600m minus $400m of debt, so $200m. Confirm the equity check and show the opening debt carrying amounts.
evals.expected_output: Total uses of $637.5m including $6.0m OID, $9.5m financing fees, $12.0m buyer deal costs and $10.0m cash; sponsor equity of $237.5m, not $200.0m; term loan carried at $286.5m and notes at $98.0m under ASC 835-30, with advisory and deal costs expensed under ASC 805-10-25-23.
expected_behavior: Must: list uses of $450.0m equity purchase price, $150.0m refinancing, $9.0m advisory, $3.0m other deal costs, $7.5m term loan arrangement fee, $2.0m notes underwriting fee, $6.0m OID (or present the term loan at $294.0m net proceeds) and $10.0m cash to balance sheet, totaling $637.5m.
Must: solve sponsor equity as $237.5m, show sources equal uses to zero, and state the $37.5m understatement in the associate's $200.0m figure.
Must: present the term loan carrying amount as $286.5m ($300.0m less $6.0m OID less $7.5m fee) and the notes as $98.0m, citing debt issuance cost presentation under ASC 835-30 (ASU 2015-03).

Must: state that the $9.0m and $3.0m acquisition-related costs are expensed by the acquirer under ASC 805-10-25-23 and are not goodwill, and that their tax deductibility (including any Rev. Proc. 2011-29 election for success-based fees) is for the tax adviser.
Must not: show the term loan at $300.0m in sources with no OID use, or omit cash to balance sheet or financing fees from uses.

evals.name: sweep-ignores-minimum-cash-and-circularity
evals.prompt: Check year 1 of our debt schedule. TLB opening balance $400.0m; amortization 1% per year of original principal; all-in rate 9.0% (Term SOFR plus margin, above the floor) on the average balance; $50.0m revolver undrawn all year with a 0.50% commitment fee. Credit agreement: ECF sweep 50%, stepping down to 25% when Consolidated Total Net Leverage is at or below 4.0x (year-1 test is 4.6x); minimum cash per the commitment papers is $25.0m. Opening cash is $25.0m. Year-1 levered free cash flow before interest and debt repayment (after taxes, capex and working capital) is $90.0m; for this exercise define ECF as that figure less cash interest and commitment fees less mandatory amortization, and treat the sweep as paid on the last day of the year. Our analyst's model uses beginning-balance interest and sweeps 100% of all cash above zero, giving a $74.75m sweep. Iterative calculation is off in the workbook. What should year 1 show?
evals.expected_output: With average-balance interest solved to convergence, interest and fees of about $34.92m, ECF of about $51.08m, a 50% sweep of about $25.54m, ending TLB of about $370.46m and ending cash of about $50.54m; the analyst's sweep wrongly uses 100%, ignores minimum cash and drains cash to zero.
expected_behavior: Must: identify that the analyst's sweep uses the wrong percentage (100% instead of 50%) and sweeps cash below the $25.0m minimum, leaving zero cash in breach of the minimum.

Must: solve the average-balance circularity (iteration with a circuit breaker or closed form) to about $34.92m of interest and fees ($34.67m term loan interest plus $0.25m commitment fee), a sweep of about $25.54m, ending TLB of about $370.46m and ending cash of about $50.54m, and show a convergence check.
Must: alternatively or additionally show the beginning-balance election (interest $36.25m, sweep about $24.88m, ending TLB about $371.13m) and label it a disclosed policy election.

Must: note that iterative calculation must be on (or the circularity removed) for average-balance interest to compute, and that real credit agreements usually pay the ECF sweep after annual financial statements, so year-end timing is a simplification.
Must: apply 1% amortization to original principal ($4.0m) and run the debt roll-forward and cash-ties checks.
Must not: accept the $74.75m sweep, or sweep cash below the minimum cash balance.

evals.name: irr-on-wrong-dates-and-exit-equals-entry
evals.prompt: Returns for Project Birch. Deal closed July 15, 2026 with $235.5m of sponsor equity at 10.0x LTM EBITDA. Add-on acquisition equity of $20.0m funded September 30, 2027. Dividend recap paid the sponsor $80.0m on June 30, 2029. Exit assumed December 31, 2031 at 10.0x LTM EBITDA of $95.0m with $350.0m of net debt, so $600.0m to the sponsor. My model puts these in annual columns 2026 to 2031 and uses =IRR(), which gives about 23.5%. We always assume exit at the entry multiple. Write up the returns for the IC deck.
evals.expected_output: Dated IRR (XIRR) of about 21.6% rather than 23.5%, MOIC of about 2.66x over about 5.47 years, the exit multiple treated as an explicit assumption with a rationale and contraction cases (about 18.1% and 2.29x at 9.0x; about 14.2% and 1.92x at 8.0x), and returns labeled gross.
expected_behavior: Must: compute IRR on the dated sponsor cash flows (-235.5 on 2026-07-15, -20.0 on 2027-09-30, +80.0 on 2029-06-30, +600.0 on 2031-12-31) and report about 21.6%, explaining that annual-period IRR overstates it because close is mid-year and the interim flows are not one year apart.
Must: report MOIC of about 2.66x ($680.0m distributions over $255.5m contributions) and a holding period of about 5.47 years.

Must: treat the 10.0x exit multiple as a policy election that needs a rationale and show at least one contraction case, such as 9.0x (about $505.0m to the sponsor, about 18.1% and 2.29x) and 8.0x (about $410.0m, about 14.2% and 1.92x).
Must: state that returns are gross of fund fees and carried interest unless net returns were modeled, and check whether management equity or exit costs reduce the $600.0m.
Must not: present 23.5% as the deal IRR, or present exit at the entry multiple as the only case.

evals.name: interest-limit-on-ebit-basis-and-book-interest
evals.prompt: Fix the tax tab in our LBO model for Calder Foods, a calendar-year C corporation acquired in a stock deal on January 2, 2026 (no basis step-up). FY2026 projections: tax EBITDA approximately $120.0m, tax depreciation and amortization $40.0m, stated cash interest $50.0m, OID accrual on the term loan $2.0m, and GAAP amortization of debt issuance costs $3.0m, so the income statement interest line is $55.0m. Gross receipts are about $900m. The analyst wrote: 163(j) ATI = EBIT under the TCJA rule from 2022, so the limit is 30% of $80.0m = $24.0m and $31.0m of the $55.0m is disallowed. The target also has $60.0m of NOLs from 2019-2023, and the model uses all of them in 2026 to wipe out taxable income. Equity value at closing was $237.5m.
evals.expected_output: Applies the EBITDA-based ATI restored for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024 (limit about $36.0m), uses business interest of $52.0m (stated interest plus OID, not the $55.0m book line), carries forward about $16.0m of disallowed interest indefinitely, and limits NOL use by the 80% rule and the Section 382 annual limit, with every figure marked for tax adviser review.
expected_behavior: Must: state that for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024 ATI adds back depreciation, amortization and depletion (Pub. L. 119-21, section 70303), so the EBIT-based rule applied only to 2022 through 2024, and approximate the FY2026 limit as 30% of about $120.0m, about $36.0m, labeled an approximation.

Must: compute business interest expense from stated interest plus OID ($52.0m), not the $55.0m book interest line, noting that the final 163(j) regulations exclude debt issuance costs from the definition of interest, with [VERIFY] where not confirmed.
Must: show about $16.0m disallowed and carried forward indefinitely, with a carryforward roll, and note the small business exemption does not apply ($32.0m 2026 gross receipts threshold).

Must: identify the acquisition as a likely Section 382 ownership change, limit annual use of pre-change NOLs to the value of the old loss corporation (about $237.5m on these facts) times the long-term tax-exempt rate for the change month, marked [VERIFY], and apply the 80% of taxable income limit to post-2017 NOLs.
Must: hand the structure and tax conclusions to analyzing-m-and-a-tax-implications or a tax adviser with the figures above.
Must not: apply the EBIT-based ATI rule to 2026, deduct the full $55.0m, or use all $60.0m of NOLs in 2026.
